newsitem.title: EGYPT: Squash-Barada beats Australian eighth seed HILL.
newsitem.headline: Squash-Barada beats Australian eighth seed HILL.

text.p: Former world junior champion Ahmed Barada defeated eighth seed Anthony Hill on a good day for the Egyptian hosts in the first round of the Gezira Open squash championship on Sunday.

Barada beat the Australian 15-6 9-15 15-8 15-10 in 46 minutes to set up a second-round clash with compatriot Amir Wagih which will guarantee Egypt at least one quarter-finalist in the $70,000 tournament.
Wagih beat Ireland's Derek Ryan 8-15 17-15 15-9 17-15 in his first-round encounter.
Fellow Egyptian Omar el Borolossy also reached the second round, thanks to a 17-16 10-15 15-5 15-5 victory over Scotland's Martin Heath, and next faces second seed Rodney Eyles of Australia.
Eyles dropped a set before overcoming Dutch qualifier Lucas Buit 15-12 11-15 15-9 15-11.
World champion Jansher Khan of Pakistan, the top seed, looked stiff and awkward in beating Finnish qualifier Juha Raumolin in straight games.
"I have been working hard for 10 days," Jansher, who was unexpectedly unable to match the pace of Eyles in the Hong Kong Open final two weeks ago, said.
Fourth seed Simon Parke of England, recovering after testicular cancer, was beaten 13-15 15-7 15-12 8-15 15-13 by Alex Gough of Wales.
